Frontend: all flows OK (locked textareas, PIN gating, wrong/right PIN, auth-notice banner on 401, sessionStorage token flow, inline account edit with server validation, welcome edit + persistence across reload, config-reset, re-lock, no CRA overlay, no console errors other than expected 401/400 from planted-garbage-token & bad-username, Tamil in footer, no horizontal overflow at 390x844). All restore invariants met (official_username=Heheheehejvjsjsjsjdjjdjdbdh, welcome_ta/en=defaults, PIN=246810, admin_attempts wiped).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py inspected: exactly one app.include_router(api_router), one CORSMiddleware block, one @app.on_event('startup'), one @app.on_event('shutdown'). No endpoint is defined twice. Fix-3 (SettingsUpdate.default='' + explicit 400 for blank welcome blocks) is correctly ordered — Pydantic no longer intercepts, clean_username raises 400 with a string first, then the blank-block guard raises 400 with a string.

client_ip() correctly prefers left-most X-Forwarded-For, then x-real-ip, then request.client.host. record_failure() upserts BOTH per-IP and __global__ buckets in a single loop; clear_failures() uses delete_many({_id: {$in: [ip, '__global__']}}) so a successful unlock wipes both. Verified end-to-end with X-Forwarded-For header manipulation.

Note: __global__ ceiling is a genuinely global counter — ANY successful unlock in the world clears it. This is fine for a single-admin bot but is worth documenting; the iter6 test therefore retries once if the counter is cleared mid-test by a concurrent successful unlock (parallel pytest worker).
